complexity_matrix.operation: Segment tree build over n elements
complexity_matrix.notes: Fewer than 2n nodes with one O(1) merge each. Construction is linear, not n log n; the logarithm applies to queries.
A contiguous range is covered by O(log n) canonical nodes because at each level at most two are partially covered.
One root-to-leaf walk recomputing one aggregate per level. Aux space is constant without recursion.
Uses lazy propagation to defer pushes to children, deferring work rather than avoiding it.

complexity_matrix.operation: Fenwick tree build from an array
complexity_matrix.notes: O(n log n) by repeated adds; O(n) with the linear in-place build that accumulates parents top-down.

complexity_matrix.operation: Fenwick prefix sum or point update
complexity_matrix.notes: One loop; the index advances by the lowest set bit, so the loop runs once per bit position.
Two prefix queries differenced. Requires an invertible aggregate, which is why range minimum is not supported.
Not supported. Minimum has no inverse, so prefix values cannot be differenced into a range value.

complexity_matrix.operation: Union-find find with path compression alone
complexity_matrix.notes: Amortised O(log n). Compression flattens paths without changing which root a node belongs to, so correctness is untouched.

complexity_matrix.operation: Union-find merge with union by rank alone
complexity_matrix.notes: Tree height bounded by log n, since a depth increment implies a component that has at least doubled.
Total cost O((n+m) alpha(n)) for m operations. Effectively constant, which is what makes near-linear algorithms feasible.
Between n and 2n slots versus the recursive layout's up to 4n, with no recursion and better locality.
sigma is the value range. Beats a segment tree on counting queries when values come from a small domain.

correctness_argument.claim: A segment tree node is correct by induction because its range is the disjoint union of its children's and the merge is associative; a query is correct because the canonical nodes it merges partition the query range exactly. Union-find preserves its equivalence classes because path compression rewrites pointers within a tree and union links only two distinct roots, so neither changes which component any element belongs to.

cost_derivations.claim: Segment tree build is Theta(n) because there are fewer than 2n nodes each doing O(1) work, while queries and updates are O(log n) because each is one root-to-leaf walk. Union-find reaches O(alpha(n)) amortised only when path compression and union by rank are combined; either alone gives only O(log n).
cost_derivations.detail: A Fenwick tree achieves O(log n) per operation in a loop of about one iteration per bit position, at exactly n+1 entries.

limits.claim: No comparison-based structure gives O(1) range queries with O(1) updates; the O(1)-query result holds only for static data after O(n) preprocessing. Union-find's near-constant bound is bought by restricting to merge-only operations, so it cannot answer connectivity after removals or path queries that exclude a vertex. The 4n segment-tree figure is a property of the recursive layout, not of the structure; the iterative layout needs between n and 2n.
